title: Monthly mean removal leaves uncertain changes above early 95th percentiles at six US gauges in 1960-1978 versus 2007-2025
abstract: We tested changes in days above early-period high-water thresholds at six US tide gauges. We compared 1960-1978 with 2007-2025 in fixed NOAA CO-OPS records. We used hourly-based daily maxima and subtracted monthly mean sea level for a separate residual test. We used early-period 95th percentiles, calendar-month weighting, and three-year block samples with refitted thresholds. Raw exceedance rates rose at all six gauges. Residual changes in percentage points were Boston -0.28, The Battery +1.08, Sewells Point +0.07, Charleston -0.03, San Francisco +0.63, Seattle -0.24. All six adjusted residual intervals included zero. A 90th-percentile check gave a positive residual change at The Battery, so the result depends on threshold scope. The package gives six-test adjusted intervals, sensitivity checks, exact source hashes, retained daily data, code, and separate arithmetic and source audits. Monthly mean removal is a descriptive filter. It does not separate tides from surges or give a causal share of change. Two selected periods, missing records, and 19 years per period limit inference.

display.caption: Change in days above early-period 95th percentiles. Left: raw daily maxima with 95% intervals. Right: maxima minus monthly mean sea level with six-test adjusted intervals. Values are percentage points.

citations.reason: Prior work separates mean level, tide, and surge contributions with hourly records. This study uses a simpler monthly filter and does not repeat that attribution method.
